messages:
olivia_peopleops: Hey team - just married and want to add my stepchild (lives with spouse overseas) during the midyear QLE. Child is on spouse's passport and doesn't have a US SSN yet. Custody is shared; spouse has primary physical custody but I have a signed custody agreement and placement letter. Can we add the stepchild now and what docs do you need? Any impact on my HSA & dependent care FSA eligibility?

ben_benefits: Congrats Olivia! You can generally add a stepchild within 60 days of a QLE (marriage). For international stepchildren without SSN we accept passport + custody/placement docs and a signed affidavit. We'll create a temporary dependent record; must provide SSN/ITIN within 120 days. HSA eligibility: adding a dependent to medical doesn't by itself change HSA eligibility unless you elect family HDHP. If you move from employee-only to family HDHP, HSA contribution limits change.

olivia_peopleops: We want to keep my current HDHP but add dependent for claims. I plan to keep HSA. Does adding a dependent force family HDHP?

ben_benefits: No - you can enroll the dependent in medical without changing your own coverage tier? Actually coverage tiers are tied to elections: if you add a dependent you must select the appropriate tier (employee + child or family). That will affect payroll contribution rates and HSA limits. If you keep employee-only HDHP but enroll dependent somewhere else, that's not supported. So you'll need to switch to the family tier for the HDHP if you want the child on the same plan. You can choose to enroll the child in a different plan offered to dependents only where applicable. Let's DM to review plan options.

mira_payroll: Heads up on payroll: switching from employee-only to family HDHP will change pre-tax deductions and HSA payroll contributions. Also dependent care FSA eligibility depends on whether the child qualifies as a dependent for tax purposes. If the child doesn't have SSN yet, we can still process FSA pre-tax elections but you'll need to provide ITIN/SSN when available for tax reporting.

kevin_tax: For Dependent Care FSA (DCFSA): the child must be a qualifying person (generally under age limits or disabled). A stepchild usually qualifies if you claim them as a dependent for tax purposes. If the child lives abroad with your spouse, residency tests can complicate dependency claiming. You should consult with a tax advisor. Also, without SSN/ITIN we can't finalize tax forms, but payroll can hold provisional deposits.

olivia_peopleops: The custody agreement states joint custody, primary physical with spouse abroad. I won't claim the child on my taxes for this year; spouse will. Can I still add for medical and DCFSA?

tara_legal: Legal note: benefits eligibility is separate from tax claiming. An employer can allow dependent coverage if documentation shows relationship and eligibility. For DCFSA, plan rules often require you to be the one incurring eligible expenses. If spouse claims the child as tax dependent, that doesn't automatically block your enrollment but affects FSA tax benefits. We'll need to review the plan SPD.

ben_benefits: Practically: we can add the stepchild to medical with these docs: passport copy, certified translation if not English, marriage certificate, stepchild custody/placement agreement, signed dependent affidavit, and a statement showing primary residence with spouse. Upload via portal -> Add dependent -> Stepchild (international).

olivia_peopleops: OK. What about retro coverage effective date? Marriage was 2026-03-05. I tried to enroll at the portal on 2026-03-20 but it rejected due to missing SSN. Submitted docs today. Can effective date be 2026-03-05?

mira_payroll: We usually set effective date as the QLE date (marriage) if docs are submitted within 60 days. Since you enrolled within 60 days, and you have proof, payroll will apply deductions retro to 03-05. If payroll cutoff passed we may do an off-cycle adjustment. Expect a reconciliation in next pay cycle.

olivia_peopleops: Any special steps for claims if child needs care before SSN is issued?

ben_benefits: We'll issue a temporary dependent ID so the provider can submit claims. Keep copies of all receipts and escalate to benefits@ if any denials. We will reconcile once SSN/ITIN is provided.

kevin_tax: FYI if you switch to family HDHP midyear, your HSA contribution limit will prorate. Mira  please confirm payroll's workflow for prorated HSA limit enforcement.

mira_payroll: Confirmed - payroll will prorate HSA limits based on the coverage tier effective dates. We enforce annual limits via year-to-date checks and will flag overcontributions. If there's an issue we'll notify the employee to adjust contributions.

olivia_peopleops: Great. I'll upload: passport, marriage cert, custody agreement, signed affidavit. Thanks all.

hrbot: Reminder: For international document uploads, include certified translations and mark the document type in the portal. Plan SPD: https://benefits.redwood.com/spd. If you need immediate help, @ben_benefits will assist with the portal upload.
